title: Challenge
description: One structured research problem, from architecture.md section 8. Generated by a validator, hash-committed before any miner runs, and private until evaluation closes. There is no simulated user and no conversational persona: a challenge is a single structured research request. Every field is integer or string so that a challenge pack hashes reproducibly.

challenge_id.description: Content address of the challenge. Derived from the challenge body, so it cannot be chosen.

domain.description: A member of the active taxonomy (section 7.2). Restricted in V1 to domains an LLM panel can inspect without a physical laboratory (section 2).

problem_statement.description: The problem as the laboratory receives it. The linter (section 7.4 step 2) rejects a challenge whose statement is not clearly stated.

research_objective.description: What a good answer must achieve. Distinct from the problem statement: the objective is what the Constraint Judge scores against (section 16.2).

current_baseline.description: How the problem is addressed today. Present so that 'materially different from prior art' has a stated reference rather than an implied one.

known_attempts.description: Approaches already tried and their outcomes. A laboratory that re-proposes one of these has not invented.

constraints.description: Hard requirements. The linter rejects a challenge with none: without constraints there is nothing for a mechanism to satisfy and nothing for the Constraint Judge to check.

forbidden_shortcuts.description: Solutions that trivially satisfy the constraints without inventing. Named explicitly so that a laboratory taking one fails the objective rather than scoring well on a technicality.

resource_limits.description: The equal budget every laboratory in the cohort receives. Equality is the control against brute-force capital (section 23).
